_: The Pixie Dust Industries brand tokens. This file is the source; site/app/brand.css is generated from it by build.mjs, and never edited by hand. The direction since 2026-10-02 is paper: uncoated stock, muted inks from Sanzo Wada's A Dictionary of Color Combinations, one quiet serif for the argument and one grotesque for everything else, one radius scale, and the fold as the single signature. It is one system from end to end, and every page reads from it. Every contrast figure here was computed, not estimated.

house.name: Pixie Dust Industries
house._: The house is Pixie Dust Industries. The thing it ships is the Product OS. The package id stays oolio-pm and the repository stays niel-cody/oolio-product-os: those are addresses, not the brand, and every installed reference depends on them.

source._: Every chromatic ink below is a named colour from the Dictionary, with the plate number it appears on in the book's own combinations. The dataset is mattdesl/dictionary-of-colour-combinations, which transcribes the book's 348 plates. Picking from one reference rather than a colour wheel is what keeps the set reading as one sheet.
source.book: Sanzo Wada, A Dictionary of Color Combinations (Seigensha, 2011 reprint of Haishoku Sōkan, 1933)

press._: A Riso runs one ink per pass. Three drums plus black is still the palette, but each drum now has two strengths, the way a plate prints at full and at a tint: the solid draws lines and small marks, the tint is the only one allowed to be a surface.

stock._: Uncoated warm grey. Riso ink is translucent, so it needs a pale sheet to sit on; the process physically cannot print on dark stock. This is why the site is light. The stock did not change: it is the thing about the old sheet worth keeping.

stock-2.use: a second sheet, lifted: cards, plates, panels, the drawer

stock-3.use: recessed, a gutter or a well, a selected row

rule.use: a hairline division inside a plate

rule-2.use: a firm division: the edge of a card, a control, a panel. Replaces the black keyline almost everywhere

drums._: One ink per pass, in order. Each has a solid and a tint. The solid may be a line, a dot, a dash, a ghost; the tint may be a ground. Neither solid pink nor yellow may ever set a word.

pink.name: Eupatorium Purple
pink.use: The dust. A dusty magenta for the loops, the misregistration ghost and the smallest marks on the page. Its tint, Corinthian Pink, is the one surface the brand allows itself: the primary button, a tag, a flash.

blue.name: Violet Blue
blue.use: The industry. A muted indigo that carries structure, links, orchestration and diagrams. The only drum besides black that may set copy. Its tint, Salvia Blue, is a cool ground for a selected or hovered thing.

yellow.name: Cream Yellow
yellow.use: The spark. Third drum, smallest budget, reserved for the human sign-off gates. As the only warm thing on the sheet, 'a person decides here' stays the loudest mark on the map. It has no tint and no other job.

k.name: Black drum
k.use: Never #000. A Riso black lays down a soft warm neutral that sits on the paper rather than punching a hole in it. All body copy runs here. It is no longer a border: a keyline in the black drum is now emphasis, used on the header rule and a section head and almost nowhere else.

tints._: Two more pale inks from the Dictionary, for the places that need a ground that is not pink or blue. A tint is a surface with black type on it, never a line.

glaucous.name: Glaucous Green
glaucous.use: a calm green ground: a passing check, an output chip

lavender.name: Grayish Lavender
lavender.use: a dusty mauve ground, between the pink and the blue

deep._: Four deep inks, each a named plate colour, for the map's meanings that need to be a line or a word. Deliberately dark so the pale stock stays pale: the colour is in the small marks, not the sheet.

olive.name: Olive Green
olive.use: an artefact the OS produced. A line or a fill with black type on it, never a word on the stock

plumbeous.name: Plumbeous
plumbeous.use: raw signal: nearly colourless, because nobody has shaped it yet

carmine.name: Carmine Red
carmine.use: destructive, failed, or unplaced. The one red on the sheet

type-colour._: What words are set in. Body copy is the black drum; everything here is a step of it, and each figure is measured on the stock.

soft-ink.use: a secondary paragraph, or long copy that should sit back

muted-ink.use: captions, eyebrows and the mono furniture. The last step that clears AA

faint-ink.use: decoration only. Never a word a person has to read

semantic._: The lifecycle map's seven meanings, each on its own ink. Colour is never the only carrier: every node also carries a badge, a gate also carries a tick, a loop is also dashed.

gate.means: a person decides here. The third drum, and the whole argument

orch.means: orchestration: a skill driving a tool. Blue carries structure

loop.means: learning returning upstream. The reason this is a system and not a pipeline, so it gets the signature ink

signal.means: raw input, before anyone has shaped it. Nearly uncoloured on purpose: colouring it would be a claim about it

moves._: One texture, and it is paper. Grain is the only move left: the halftone washes, the overprint blend and the misregistration ghosts of the first press were retired on 2026-10-02 because they read as a filter over the page rather than as the page. The sheet is calm, and the ink sits on it once.

grain.how: fractalNoise at baseFrequency 0.82, four octaves, multiplied over the page in one position:fixed pass
grain.why: Fixed, so it never scrolls with the content: the sheet stays still while the ink moves. Eight per cent is uncoated paper under a lamp. Anything higher starts to read as dirt.

retired.halftone: 2026-10-02. Screens of dots behind the hero card and the systems map: a pattern, not a print.
retired.overprint: 2026-10-02. Existed only to blend the halftone plates.
retired.misregistration: 2026-10-02. Two coloured ghosts behind a headline read as shouting. You cannot cut a sheet of paper twice.

type._: Mincho and Gothic: a quiet serif for the argument and a precise grotesque for everything a person reads or clicks, which is the classic Japanese pairing and the calmest one there is. Three faces, one job each, and every page uses the same three in the same roles.

display.use: the argument: page titles, section lines, the wordmark. Regular weight, never bold. The optical-size axis lets it set small without going spindly

text.use: everything a person reads or clicks. Precise, neutral, built for interfaces, doing nothing interesting on purpose so the serif can

system.use: every label, count, stamp and slash command. The one piece of furniture that does not vary

shape._: One radius scale, three steps, and every element on every page takes one of them: small for a chip, a code span or a tag; control for every button, input and selectable row; surface for every card, panel, tile and drawer. No pills. The fold is the signature: a dog-ear on the top right corner of a surface that holds content, drawn in the stock and the pink tint, never on a control.

fold.why: A sheet with one corner turned shows what it is made of. One per surface, top right, never on a control, never bigger than the type beside it.

out.use: a plate settling: entering and exiting

motion._noEaseIn: There is deliberately no ease-in. It delays the moment being watched most, which is what makes an interface feel sluggish at an identical duration.

mark._: The Gate, re-inked again. The ring is the loop, the break is where it does not close on its own, and the bead is the person who closes it. The bead is Cream Yellow because that is the human-gate drum, so the meaning survives the change of palette intact.
mark.clearSpace: one bead diameter (6 units on the 32 grid) on every side

aliases._: The names the site already speaks, kept pointing at the right ink so no component had to be rewritten to be reprinted.
